narrative:
Based on the information available, the model has assessed a 31% probability that you would default on this loan. In practical terms, this means that, among applicants with a very similar profile, roughly 31 out of 100 would fail to repay. Given the bank’s risk tolerance, that level of uncertainty is too high, and the application has therefore been denied.

Several aspects of your profile worked in your favor. Having over 1,000 DM in your savings account is actually rare among approved borrowers—only about 3% have that much saved—and this had the strongest positive influence on your evaluation. It signals that you have a financial cushion. Your stable employment of seven or more years, your own home, and the fact that you have no other installment plans are also positive signals.

However, two factors weighed more heavily against you. First, the purpose of the loan—a new car—is not as common among approved applicants. Only about 16.5% of approved loans were for new cars, and this type of purchase appears to carry more perceived risk. Second, your checking account balance, which sits between 0 and 200 DM, is relatively modest. Most approved applicants have no checking account balance at all, but among those who do, a balance in this range is less frequent and was interpreted as a sign of tighter day-to-day finances.

To improve your chances in the future, consider building up your checking account balance, saving even more if possible, or reconsidering the loan’s purpose. Your impressive savings are a strong foundation—combining them with stronger checking account activity and a less risky loan purpose could make a significant difference.
